title_en: With Whom One Should Not Make Enmity
translation:
Ramayan: the episode of the dialogue between Ravan and Marich.

There are nine [with whom one should not make enmity]: 1) Shastri, 2) Marmi, 3) Prabhu, 4) Sath, 5) Dhani, 6) Vaidya, 7) Bandi, 8) Kavi, 9) Kovid.

1) Shastri — one who carries weapons. 2) Marmi — one who knows [another's] merits and faults. 3) Prabhu — a master. 4) Sath — a fool, who watches for a chance to strike alone, to set a fire, to give poison, and the like. 5) Dhani — a wealthy man can do whatever he pleases [against you]. 6) Vaidya — a physician can prescribe what is harmful. 7) Bandi — a bard/flatterer spreads heavy slander. 8) Kavi — a poet [unclear] can bring harm through verse. 9) Kovid — a learned pandit can destroy [one] through spells of death and delusion (marana-mohan vidya). One should not make enmity with these nine enemies as described above.

_Kabir sant sohagi ramke, shabde uthe jaag, salil shabdse nahi, jar uthe ban aag._ (Servant Kabir says: saints who are devoted lovers of Ram become alert and awaken on hearing the sound of Ram's name; but the wicked/worldly person [salil], hearing that same sound, blazes up in anger like fire.)

_Pathato nasti murkhatvam, japato nasti patakam, mounina kalaho nasti, na bhayam chasti jagratah._ (One who studies has no foolishness in him. One who does namasmaran [recitation of the divine name] carries no sin. One who keeps silence has no quarrel. And one who remains alert and watchful has no fear.)

_Kshudhitastrishitah kami vidyarthi bahuposhakah, bhandari rakshakashchaiva sapta suptanprabodhakah._ (The hungry one, the thirsty one, the lustful one, the student, one who supports many, the storekeeper, and the watchman — these seven should be awakened if found sleeping.)

_Ya nisha sarvabhutanam tasyam jagarti sanyami, yasyam jagrati bhutani sa nisha pashyato muneh. ||69||_ (Gita, ch. 2) (That which is night for all beings — in that the self-controlled one keeps awake; and that in which [other] beings are awake [to sense-pleasures] is night for the sage who beholds the Supreme.)

Rekhta (page 180, Volume No. 62).

_Sovta hai to jagya hai bapda, jagta sovta kahan jage. Mani man mahi gyani huva, sabad avdhutaka kaha lage. Kahat aru sunat sab avadhi hui, anapayani bhakti nahi hath aai. Kahat Kabir ih gyan sab thothra, jivka bhala kyun hoi bhoi._ (If a person is truly asleep, poor fellow, he will wake at a shout; but one who feigns sleep while actually awake — how can he be woken? One who has, in his own mind, taken himself to be a knower — how can the teaching of a soul absorbed in God have any effect on him? By merely speaking of it and hearing of it, while his allotted span of life runs out, he never attains unshakeable, unchanging devotion. Kabir says: all such [pretended] knowledge is hollow — how then can such a soul ever find its welfare?)

A Harijan (devotee of Hari) who has thus risen and awakened from this daily dissolution (nitya pralaya) is, as it were, born anew. One should embrace and meet a Harijan warmly, for that brings about a second birth; therefore, through one saint meeting another, and through uttering "Ramkabir," that devotee becomes fulfilled — but only if he also sings the glories of Govind; without that, that is, without the kirtan (hymn-singing) of Keshav, merely passing the time brings no success. A sakhi (couplet):

_Kabir harijan aavat dekhkar, uthkar so maliye sadh, mansa vacha karmana, mite koti aparadh._ (Servant Kabir says: on seeing a Harijan approaching, rise and go meet that saint; by meeting him in thought, word, and deed, our millions of sins are erased.)

In turn, Jivandasji said that this has been called the daily dissolution. Now, in the great dissolution (mahapralaya), when the individual soul escapes from the mouth of Time — if it does not then attain Vasudevji, it falls once more into the mouth of the Time of the great dissolution. The words of Adhyaruji:

_Kshanu kshanu janme ne kshanu mare, (swami) chadhe kaalne hath, thaam thaam kare maaheru, te nahi aave saath, payelagi kar vinati._ (The body is born and dies at every single moment, and falls into the grip of Time. The life within it keeps claiming "mine, mine" over this place and that, but none of it goes along with it [when it departs].)

So Vaishnav Jivandasji said that this dissolution is such that, in the three worlds, Time has devoured the whole world except the Harijans. Every moment [beings] were born, and every moment they died; from one kalpa (cosmic age) to the next, right up to [the final] kalpa, they kept dying and being born, yet they never worshipped the Lord. A sakhi:

_Kabir chinta to harinamki, or na chitpe daas, je kachhu chitve ram bina, sohi kaalse paas._ (Servant Kabir says: O devotees, be concerned only with the remembrance of the Lord's name; devotees should be concerned with nothing else. Whoever gives thought to anything other than Ram falls into the grip of Time.)

Thus Adhyaruji says:

_Aharnish sant sangat karo, pahor ghadi anumesh, dhyan dhariney joiye re, dise tara vesh._ (Keep the company of saints day and night; do not give up their company even for a watch, an hour, or the blink of an eye. For if we look with deep reflection, our own true self is seen manifest in those saints.)

Kabirji further said, in Mal Godi (Sarang):

_Rameiya hari gun gaiye, paiye param nidhan, Rameiya hari gun gaiye. ||Tek||_
_Akare jug upaje re, tikare jug jaay, anahad ben bajai le, prabhu mahara rahyo re gagan math chhaay. ||1||_
_Juthe jug dahekyo ghanu re, kaha jivanki aas, ram rasayan je pie, taku bohor na duji pyaas. ||2||_
_Adakshanu jivyo bhalo re, hoy hari bhagtansu het, kot kalp jivyo vritha, taathe nahi mere harjisu het. ||3||_
_Kaha bhasam lepan jata re, kaha guphame vaas, man jite jug jitiye, taathe vakhya fare re udaas. ||4||_
_Kaha jap tap sanjama re, kaha tirath vrat asnaan, ene joge jugat na paiye, taathe bhaav bhakt bhagvaan. ||5||_
_Sampat dekhi na harkhiye, vipat na mariye roe, jaanhaan sampat taanhaan vipat here, raja ram kare so hoy. ||6||_
_Sarag vaas na vanchhiye re, na dariye narak nivaas, honaar so hoega, taathe juthi e mankee aas. ||7||_
_Shunya mandalme shodhi le re, hari prem jot prakaash, jaako roop na rekh he re, bin phule phalo re akaash. ||8||_
_Kahet kabir hari shodhi le re, sant rudia manjhaar, jaanhaan sevak seva kare re, ta sang rame re moraar. ||9||_

(O soul, sing the praise of Ram's divine glories, and thereby attain the supreme treasure — sing the praise of Hari. [Refrain]
1. From the manifest form [sagun-sakar] this world arises, and through transformation the world passes away; so keep sounding the unstruck word ceaselessly — my Lord abides, pervading the inner, celestial abode.
2. The soul has been deceived a great deal by this false, illusory age — what trust is there in this life? One who has drunk the elixir of Ram no longer thirsts for any other taste.
3. Better to have lived even half a moment in this world with loving affection for Hari's devotees, than to have lived for millions of kalpas in vain, without love for my Lord Hari.
4. What use is smearing oneself with ashes, or growing matted locks? What use is dwelling in a cave? If one conquers the mind, one conquers the world, and thereby [worldly] desires themselves grow weary and depart.
5. What use is japa, tapa (austerity), or self-restraint? What use is pilgrimage, vows, or ritual bathing? By such practices alone one does not find the right method — through them, loving devotion to God is not attained.
6. Do not rejoice on seeing prosperity, nor weep and wail on seeing misfortune; for wherever there is prosperity, misfortune lurks there too — remain content in whatever King Ram ordains.
7. Do not long to dwell in heaven, nor fear to dwell in hell; whatever is destined will happen — so the mind's hopes and cravings are false.
8. Seek out, in the empty, uninhabited expanse, the manifest radiance of Hari's love — He who has no form or mark, who blossoms and fruits without flower or fruit, pervading the whole sky.
9. Kabir says: seek out this Hari within the heart, there where saints dwell — wherever a devoted servant renders service, there Morar [Krishna] plays alongside him.)

Thus the soul, confined within the body which is like a cage of karma, dissolves moment by moment in this daily dissolution; but if it finds a Guru, the Guru shows it the way to be freed from bondage to the qualities of the senses, and by meeting one's true Guru (sadguru), through the company of saints, it attains the realization of God.
